title: Diabetes Mellitus
subtitle: A chronic metabolic disease characterized by elevated blood glucose levels resulting from defects in insulin production, insulin action, or both.

sections.title: Symptoms
sections.intro: Diabetes affects over 500 million people worldwide. While it cannot be cured, it can be managed effectively with lifestyle changes, medication, and regular monitoring to prevent serious complications.
items: Frequent urination (polyuria) especially at night
Excessive thirst (polydipsia)
Unexplained weight loss (especially Type 1)
Blurred vision and slow-healing wounds
Frequent infections (skin, gum, urinary tract)
Tingling or numbness in hands and feet

sections.title: Causes
sections.intro: Diabetes occurs when the pancreas does not produce enough insulin or the body cannot effectively use the insulin it produces.
items: Type 1, Autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing beta cells
Type 2, Insulin resistance combined with progressive beta cell failure
Gestational diabetes, during pregnancy due to hormonal changes
Genetic factors, obesity, sedentary lifestyle increase Type 2 risk

sections.title: Prevention
items: Maintain a healthy weight, even 5-10% weight loss improves blood sugar
Eat a balanced diet low in refined carbohydrates and sugar
Exercise for at least 150 minutes per week
Get regular blood sugar screenings if overweight or over 45
Avoid smoking and limit alcohol consumption
Manage stress, stress hormones raise blood sugar

sections.title: Treatment
items: Lifestyle changes: healthy diet, exercise, weight management
Metformin, first-line medication for Type 2 diabetes
Insulin therapy, essential for Type 1, used in advanced Type 2
SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 agonists for Type 2
Regular HbA1c, blood pressure, and cholesterol monitoring
Foot care and annual eye exams to detect complications early

facts: Over 537 million adults living with diabetes (2021)
Heart disease, kidney failure, blindness, amputations
